name: Vancouver
industries: Port logistics, mining headquarters, film and visual effects, and a livability-driven tech scene share the project market.
intro:
Vancouver's project market mixes Pacific trade with Hollywood North: the port — Canada's largest — runs continuous infrastructure programs, the film and visual-effects industry manages production at industrial scale, and a tech scene anchored by global engineering offices keeps growing on livability migration. Mining headquarters add capital-program demand. PMP serves the port, mining and construction world; Scrum credentials carry the tech and creative-tech sector. There are live online batches all year for Vancouver — pick a Saturday–Sunday weekend or a Wednesday–Thursday weekday cohort — each timed to fall within normal Vancouver working-day hours; the schedule below gives the precise local start and end for every date. Throughout: live instruction over one weekend, exam application help, realistic mocks, and trainer access until certification.

Vancouver's project mix is distinctly Pacific: film and visual-effects pipelines running studio-scale delivery, a tech sector hiring for both local product and US-remote roles, and the port and resource-sector programs that anchor the province. US-adjacent hiring makes globally recognized certification especially portable here. Training runs live online across two consecutive days shown in Vancouver local time on this page. BC compensation trails Toronto less for certified roles than general averages suggest; the sourced Vancouver entries below give this market's own dated figures. The employer list shows the film-tech-resource spread hiring certified professionals, and studios or scale-ups can certify delivery leads together via private cohorts.
